correctness.rationale: An element I+N(a,b,c,d,e,h) is square-one iff ab=bc=ae+dc=0; pairwise commutation adds ab′=a′b,bc′=b′c,ae′+dc′=a′e+d′c. In an m-tuple with B-vector nonzero, proportionality and b_i² constraints force all A,C=0, giving (q^m−1)q^(3m) with arbitrary d,e,h. If B=0, each (a,c,d,e) is singular for hyperbolic Q=ae+dc and pairwise totally isotropic, hence has span dimension<=2. Rank-one 2x2 determinantal matrices give (q+1)^2 singular projective points and two rulings of 2(q+1) maximal totally singular planes. Counting ordered m-tuples of each rank by ∏_{j=0}^{r−1}(q^m−q^j), multiplying by free h choices, gives polynomial formula, valid also m=0. Binomial inversion removes identity coordinates. Every elementary abelian subgroup with any b≠0 lies in H (order q^4); otherwise it lies in K_W for some maximal singular 2-plane, only K_W0 is contained in H, leaving 2q+1 maximal order-q^3 groups. This holds for abstract F2-linear subgroups without assuming all are Fq-subspaces. Fresh direct q=2 group brute yielded C1=28,C2=448,C3=6112; source checker q=4 C1=496,C2=96256; tests corroborate, not prove all q,m.
